newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal sees speciality chemical growth.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal sees speciality chemical growth.

text.p: AlliedSignal Inc expects to double the size of its $500 million specialty chemicals business by the year 2000 through globalization, new product development, acquisitions, and improved operational efficiency, AlliedSignal Specialty Chemicals president David C. Hill said Tuesday.
The specialty chemicals unit, headquartered in Seelze, Germany, said Norbert Dieterich has joined AlliedSignal as head of its Riedel-de Haen business unit.
Prior to joining AlliedSignal, Dieterich was chief executive of American Home Products Corp's German agricultural chemicals and pesticides business, Cyanamid Agrar GmbH und Co KG.
He now serves as chairman of Riedel-de Haen's executive board, with responsibility for the business unit's technology, production and business support functions.
Dieterich reports to David C. Hill, previous chairman of Riedel-de Haen's executive board. AlliedSignal said.
Hill remains on the board but will devote more time in Seelze to finalizing and implementing AlliedSignal's growth strategy to be a leading global market-based specialty chemicals business.

It said the strategy will focus on markets where it can achieve critical mass, such as: pharmaceutical and agricultural chemicals; plastic and polymer additives; chemicals for the paint and coatings industry; chemicals for the sealants and adhesives industry; chemicals for the electronics industry and industrial chemicals.
